title: 自動制御
subtitle: Automatic Control
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn framework of feedback control theory involving "Mathematical Expression","Laplace Conversions","Block Diagrams","Transfer Functions" and furthermore
(2) learn characteristics  "Transfer Functions","Stability","Transient & Frequency Responses","Steady States".
advice:
This is a basic course of Feedback Control. We will cover the following materials:

1. Basic concepts in feedback control: System elements and block diagram, representation with elementary blocks.
2. The various elements of a control process: Proportional, integrating, differentiating, 1st-order, 2nd-order,
   and delya-time lag blocks.
3. Transformation from time to frequency domains: The elementary blocks and the transfer functions. The Laplace
   transformation and the transfer functions. Examples of electric circuit systems.
4. Transfer characteristics of typical basic blocks: Specifications in the time domain (transient responses) and
   the frequency domain(frequency responses). The Lablace inversion and the time funcsions, Graphical resprese-
   ntation by the frequency functions.
5. Stability of linear control systems: The concept of stabiity, stability analysis using the Routh-Hurwitz
   crierion (matrices & determininants)
6. Desing of PI-control systems: Design method of the basic PI-control systems.
books:
Textbook: 実務者のためのPID制御設計[森北出版]
Reference books: やさしく学べる制御工学[森北出版]、わかる自動制御（増補改訂版）[日新出版]、システム設計のための基礎制御工学[コロナ社]
requiredKnowledge:
Acquisition of “Computer Engineering for Electrical Engineers” and “Electrical and Electronic Instrumentation”.
Enough skill of mathematics (especially matrix / inverse matrix and determinant calculations).
Basic knowledge of mathematics (the Laplace conversion & inversion and so on).
How to use a calculator.

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1) Explain more than six elementary blocks of a control process and their characteristics.
(2) Perform the Laplace conversions & inversions for the transfer functions that play key roles in complicated control systems.
(3) Express the transfer elements in the frequency (s) domain for some electric circuit models.
(4) Calculate and characterize the transient and frequency responses of the transfer functions in the complicated control systems.
achievementLevels.standard:
(1) Explain some basic elements of a control process and their characteristics.
(2) Perform the Laplace conversions & inversions for the elementary transfer functions using mathematical formulas.
(3) Express the transfer functions of control systems in block diagrams.
(4) Explain transient responses to noise signals and their stabilities, and analyze them using the Routh-Hurwitz criterion.
